newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell off Cerrejon coal mine at end-97.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell off Cerrejon coal mine at end-97.

text.p: The Colombian government announced Wednesday it would sell its 50 percent stake in the Cerrejon coal mine in northern Colombia in December 1997.
At present it operates the mine jointly with a local subsidiary of Exxon Corp.
In addition, a government spokesman said Colombia's coal reserves currently stand at 6.63 billion metric tonnes.
The government has not yet prepared any estimate of how much it expects to receive for the sale of its stake in the mine in the sparsely populated province of Guajira.

Guajira and neighboring Cesar province have a total of 18 mines, five of which are considered as large mining operations and the remaining 13 as medium-sized. They produced a combined total of 20 million metric tonnes in 1995.
The northern zone of Cerrejon, where the government and Exxon-owned mine is situated, has reserves of three billion metric tonnes but only 921 million tonnes are thought to be recoverable.
